audit.title: Chainlink Functions Billing

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Sections open reasonably ("To send Chainlink Functions requests, you must maintain a sufficient amount of LINK…"), but there is no top-of-page TL;DR stating the two-step estimate→charge model in one liftable sentence. The billing model is explained across two numbered steps rather than a single canonical statement.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; clean H2/H3/H4 hierarchy, 0 level skips, 9 tables, all sections under 600 words (max 418). No action needed.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong; 46 numerals per 1k words with worked figures (9 gwei, 300000 callback gas limit, 320 cents USD premium, 0.78 LINK reserved). Minor weakness: "performs several accounting movements" is vague where a specific would help.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Adequate internal linking (architecture, Price Feeds, Supported Networks) and 3 external links to `data.chain.link` feeds, but 0 links to primary sources — no link to the FunctionsRouter/FunctionsCoordinator contract source or a spec for `handleOracleFulfillment`.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Decent inline definitions ("Premium fees: These fees are paid in LINK to compensate nodes…"), but key terms like "subscription reservation" and "request threshold" are used before a crisp standalone definition.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weakest dimension: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no `datePublished`/`dateModified`, no og/twitter tags (per measured facts). Head metadata could not be independently verified — the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read — but the served HTML carries no structured signals.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: The 2 fenced blocks are billing formulas, both untagged. No actual runnable code (no address, no contract call example for `getConfig`). For a billing page this is expected, but tagging the fences and adding a concrete `getConfig` call snippet would help agents.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Good lifecycle coverage (request cost → reservation → fulfillment → secrets minimum → withdrawal/cancellation), but no symptom/error-phrased headings ("Why was more LINK reserved than charged?", "Why did I get charged a cancellation fee?") that match how devs actually search.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent product/entity naming (FunctionsRouter, FunctionsCoordinator, DON) and unambiguous prose. No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a well-structured billing reference for Chainlink Functions with strong worked examples: two full cost-calculation walkthroughs, 9 tables, and 68 numerals with real gwei/LINK/USD figures. Its biggest GEO strength is concrete, quotable arithmetic (a request costing "0.2425 LINK" is exactly the kind of specific an engine cites). Its biggest opportunity is discoverability: no JSON-LD/`TechArticle` schema, missing canonical URL, no dates, and no summary sentence answering the top query — "how much does a Chainlink Functions request cost and how is it billed." The honest verdict: solid content that is under-instrumented for retrieval and lacks a liftable top-line answer.

recommendations.title: Add structured metadata (`TechArticle` JSON-LD + canonical + dateModified)
recommendations.issue: measured facts — "JSON-LD: 0 block(s)… canonical: MISSING… dateModified absent"
recommendations.change: emit a `TechArticle` JSON-LD block with `headline`, `dateModified`, `about: "Chainlink Functions billing"`, and a self-referential canonical URL.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and visible freshness are direct trust/parse signals for agents; absence caps this dimension.

recommendations.title: Add an answer-first TL;DR of the billing model
recommendations.where: immediately under `# Chainlink Functions Billing`, before "Request costs"
recommendations.issue: page opens into mechanics with no one-line summary of cost = gas + premium.
recommendations.change: add one liftable sentence, e.g. "A Chainlink Functions request costs gas cost + a USD-denominated premium fee, both paid in LINK from your subscription; the maximum is reserved at request time and the exact amount is charged at fulfillment."
recommendations.why: a crisp self-contained claim is what engines quote verbatim and defends against skimmed/parametric answers.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased headings for common billing questions
recommendations.where: new H3s under relevant sections or a short FAQ
recommendations.issue: no headings matching "why was I charged less than reserved" or "why a cancellation fee."
recommendations.change: add H3s like "Why is the reserved amount larger than the final charge?" (answer: 99% gas-fluctuation overestimation) and "Why did canceling my subscription incur a fee?" (answer: below request threshold).
recommendations.why: symptom-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses, even when the answer is already in body text.

recommendations.title: Tag the formula code fences and add a concrete `getConfig` example
recommendations.where: the two formula blocks and the fallback-ratio paragraph
recommendations.issue: measured facts — "2 fenced block(s)… 2 untagged"; `getConfig` mentioned but not shown.
recommendations.change: tag fences (e.g. ```` ```text ````) and add a short labeled snippet showing a `getConfig` call on FunctionsCoordinator returning the fallback Wei→LINK ratio.
recommendations.why: labeled, runnable snippets are easier for agents to parse and execute.

recommendations.title: Link claims to primary sources
recommendations.change: add inline links to the FunctionsRouter/FunctionsCoordinator contract source or reference API page and to the `handleOracleFulfillment` interface.
recommendations.why: primary-source links raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifier with a specific
recommendations.change: enumerate the movements (release reservation, deduct gas cost, deduct premium) or link to the reference detailing them.
recommendations.why: specifics outperform qualitative-only prose in generative answers.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifier: "performs several accounting movements" (measured facts flag "several").
Untagged code fences (2 of 2) — minor parse-friendliness loss.
No stale-content risk visible in prose, but absence of any `dateModified` means freshness is unverifiable to an engine.
offPageNotes: JSON-LD, canonical, and freshness signals are largely template/site-level — coordinate with the docs platform, not just this page.
The page already references `/llms.txt`; ensure this billing URL is listed there for agent discovery.
Blockchain-specific values (minimum balance, request threshold, cancellation fee) live on the Supported Networks page — ensure that page cross-links back here to reinforce the canonical-hub pattern.
